title: Quantification of autophagy flux in isolated mouse skeletal muscle fibers with overexpression of fluorescent protein mCherry-EGFP-LC3
protocol: Inject anesthetized mice with 10 μL of 2 mg/mL hyaluronidase dissolved in sterile saline at the ventral side of the hind paws using a 29-gauge needle.
Wait one hour and then inject 20 μL (2 mg/mL) mCherry-EGFP-LC3 plasmid DNA in autoclaved ddH2O at the same site of hyaluronidase injection.
Place two electrodes about 10 mm apart at the starting lines separating paw and toes, fifteen minutes after DNA injection.
Apply twenty-five pulses of 100 V/cm electric field at 20 ms bursts with 1 s burst interval under LV mode.
On day 8, inject colchicine (0.4 mg/kg) intraperitoneally into the mice.
Surgically remove FDB muscles and place in Tyrode solution on day 10.
Place the FDB muscle inside a tube with 1 mL digestion solution and incubate for 40 min at 37°C in a shaking incubator.
Dissociate the FDB fibers by passing through a series of pipettes with decreasing diameter.
Plate the FDB fibers onto glass-bottomed dishes filled with Tyrode solution.
Place the glass-bottomed dish on the dish holder of the confocal microscope.
Image the intact FDB fibers using a Zeiss 780 confocal microscope with a 20× objective lens.
Excite EGFP and mCherry using 488 nm and 594 nm lasers, respectively.
Capture images at 2048*2048 scanning resolution.
Save all images as original CZI files.
Use a homemade ImageJ macro (FFTmuscle.ijm) for batch processing on a single input folder of images.
Process and generate processed images with the program.
Output results into a new folder within the user-selected directory.
Use entire images for analysis to avoid cherry-picking.
Ensure image resolution reaches several pixels per punctum to distinguish from random noise across the image.
Adjust ImageJ macro codes based on specific imaging settings to select green or red channel.
Define patterns of basal fluorescence that are repetitive in nature using FFT.
Remove defined patterns of basal fluorescence.
Reconstruct fluorescence image after subtraction of baseline fluorescence for single FDB muscle fiber.
Select the condensed segments above or below the center point of the FFT image that represent the repetitive striated pattern.
Wipe the rectangle area containing the selected segments to black in the FFT image.
Set foreground and background colors to White/Black in ImageJ.
Repeat the steps to delete other condensed segments above or below the center point.
Click the “OK” button on the waiting user window to proceed to the quantification step.
Perform inverse FFT to generate processed images containing condensed GFP-positive puncta.
Save the image in the output folder.
Repeat steps 7–9 for the RED channel.
Generate a merged image of GFP and RFP once both GREEN and RED channel analyses are complete.
Open a new window showing the total count and total area of GFP and RFP positive puncta.
Determine the average size for the given frame as the total area/count.
Process the next image until all images in the input folder are analyzed.
Save the summary results.
Open the file in Excel for further statistical evaluation.
